trust_decision.summary: The untrusted input is an embedded PostScript program stream, so the interpreter must bound attacker-controlled sizes before allocating and before recursing: the `array` operand, the `for` iteration space, and user-dictionary name expansion. IMPORTANT: the first published fix commit is ALREADY PRESENT in the pinned tree (PSOperator.java:38-39,541,592 and Type1FontProgram.java:57,195 match the post-image of 73d6ec0 exactly, including the `depth >` form that cb35386 later changed to `depth >=`), so the flaw the advisory closes has no reproducible path at this pin; the only live resource sink on the same mechanism is the unbounded Type 4 procedure nesting and the per-operator (not per-parse) caps.

landing_point.why: The advisory names PostScript Type 1 font programs, so an engineer looks first at Type1FontProgram.parseFont, which tokenises the embedded font program and dispatches each object through processObject/toExecute.

fix_sites.entry_point: PDType1Font.getFontProgram (PDType1Font.java:121-151) -> new Type1FontProgram -> parseFont -> processObject -> `array` operator; also CMapFactory.getCMap (CMapFactory.java:50-61) -> CMapParser.parse -> `array`
fix_sites.module_kind: shared PostScript operator interpreter in the lower-level parser package

fix_sites.entry_point: PDType1Font.getFontProgram -> Type1FontProgram.parseFont -> processObject -> `for` operator; also CMapFactory.getCMap -> CMapParser.parse -> `for`
fix_sites.module_kind: shared PostScript operator interpreter in the lower-level parser package
PD-layer font program parser (the module named by the advisory)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is titled around Type 1 font programs, so a solver can treat the shared PSOperator vocabulary as font-only machinery and reason that CMap streams and Type 4 function streams are different PDF objects with their own parsers, never noticing that the same interpreter and the same sink are shared.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A `for` with increment 0, or with initial/limit in the wrong direction for the increment sign, is a legal do-nothing loop that real Type 1 fonts contain; the published first commit made it throw (PSOperator.java:588-590) and the follow-up commit had to downgrade it to a logged warning plus skipping the loop, otherwise legitimate font programs stop parsing.

O6_input_shapes: array operand larger than the int range (truncated by intValue before the first fix; the follow-up keeps it as Long)
for with initial greater than limit for a positive increment, or initial less than limit for a negative increment
for with an iteration count above the cap (e.g. 0 1 1000000000)
self-referential user-dictionary entries reached through recursive name expansion in toExecute

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Type 4 function streams parse arbitrarily nested `{ }` procedures with an unguarded recursive call and no depth limit; FunctionParser accepts every brace as an operator so nesting depth is attacker-controlled.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Type 4 functions are not Type 1 font programs and live in a different package, so the font-program scope of the advisory appears not to cover them.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another package (org.verapdf.pd.function) plus org.verapdf.parser.FunctionParser; two files away from the Type 1 landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The array/for caps are per-operator, not per-parse, so one font program can run a 10_000-iteration `for` whose body executes `65536 array` and still allocate on the order of 6.5e8 COSObjects; no aggregate budget is enforced anywhere in the parse.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Each individual operator already sits inside the published limits, so a solver can say the published protection is applied and the composite case is a different, unspecified issue.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as a fix site; the composite only appears when the two capped operators are combined through a procedure body

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A CMap consumer that executes the same PSOperator vocabulary (`array`, `for`, `dict`, `def`) with no per-parse budget of its own.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: CMaps are PostScript-syntax streams embedded in PDFs and this parser already reuses PSParser/PSOperator directly, so a maintainer hardening the font path would plausibly leave this consumer unhardened.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Nested-procedure parser with recursive descent and no depth counter.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same interpreter machinery and same author-facing pattern as Type1FontProgram.toExecute, so the same guard would naturally be duplicated here by a maintainer following the advisory.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: eexec private-dictionary loops driven by attacker-declared counts (amountOfGlyphs, amountOfSubrs) with per-entry allocation and no cap on the declared count.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is in the same Type 1 file family and the counts are read straight from the stream, so a maintainer fixing Type 1 allocation limits could have added a bound here too.

O9_family: Improperly controlled sequential memory allocation (CWE-1325) / unbounded resource consumption inside an embedded PostScript interpreter

O10_build.toolchain: Maven; parent verapdf-parent 1.31.1 is resolved from artifactory.openpreservation.org (vera-dev); jacoco + surefire plugins
O10_build.project_tests: JUnit 5 (junit-jupiter-params) and JUnit 4 under src/test/java: PDType4FunctionTest exercises Type 4 operator execution, CMapTest exercises CMap parsing, TrueType/OpenType/parser/filter tests exist; there is no test for Type1FontProgram or for the PSOperator caps.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Cap only the `array` size (or only the length of the font program stream) and stop, leaving `for` iteration, recursive name expansion and the per-parse aggregate unbounded.
